think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 40-year-old male presents with acute-on-chronic right upper quadrant and epigastric pain following strenuous physical exertion (weightlifting), accompanied by anorexia, nausea, sudden fever, abdominal distension, and right flank tenderness. Cross-sectional imaging identified a massive 25 cm x 21 cm x 14 cm complex cystic and solid lesion with ascites, strongly mimicking an intra-abdominal malignant neoplasm rather than classical cystic hydatid disease.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs after initial emergency evaluation, baseline laboratory tests demonstrating mild leukocytosis, and abdominal ultrasound/CT imaging defining the organ displacement and cystic-solid mass, immediately prior to exploratory laparotomy and intraoperative fluid microscopy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Cystic abdominal or hepatic malignancy (such as cystadenoma/cystadenocarcinoma) was considered based on the solid-appearing pseudotumor morphology and extensive ascites, but excluded intraoperatively by the lack of neoplastic tissue and presence of daughter vesiculae. Pyogenic liver abscess or bacterial peritonitis was considered given fever and leukocytosis, but disproven by negative bacterial cultures. Microscopic examination of cystic aspirate revealing diagnostic hooklets confirmed echinococcosis.
case_prompt:
A 40-year-old man presented to the hospital with right upper quadrant and epigastric pain that began 20 days prior following weightlifting, accompanied by nausea and anorexia. One day prior to admission, he developed an acute fever. He had no history of chronic liver disease, jaundice, or changes in bowel habits.

On physical examination, the abdomen was enlarged with dullness to percussion without shifting dullness, and tenderness was elicited in the right flank. Laboratory evaluation was notable for mild leukocytosis, with otherwise normal initial routine blood tests.

Abdominal ultrasonography revealed a large (>10 cm), solid, hyperechoic cystic lesion with a heterogeneous pseudotumor appearance, accompanied by a large volume of perihepatic, intraperitoneal, and pelvic ascitic fluid. The gallbladder appeared normal, and no other focal lesions were identified. Abdominal computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a 25 cm x 21 cm x 14 cm cystic mass strongly adherent to the anterior aspect of the right hepatic lobe, occupying the entire right and median abdominal cavity, displacing bowel loops to the left, and extending into the pelvis.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Suspected preoperatively due to the solid-cystic pseudotumoral appearance on ultrasound and extensive peritoneal fluid, but excluded intraoperatively when the lesion was shown to be an exophytic cyst filled with daughter cysts and nonpurulent gelatinous matrix without neoplastic tissue.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Further diagnostic evaluation raised the clinical suspicion of abdominal malignancy. On the abdominal ultrasonography, there was a large >10 cm, solid, hyperechogenic, cystic lesion with heterogeneous pseudotumor appearance and presence of large amount of perihepatic, intraperitoneal, and pelvic ascitic fluid nonpathognomonic of hydatid disease.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the abrupt onset of fever, right flank tenderness, leukocytosis, and peritoneal fluid collection, but intraoperative aspirate cultures were negative for bacterial growth.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The cultures that were obtained intraoperatively from this fluid were negative for bacterial infection.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Surgical exploration revealed a huge exophytic hepatic cyst packed with daughter vesiculae and gelatinous matrix, and microscopic fluid examination confirmed characteristic parasitic hooklets.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Microscopy of the cystic fluid showed hooklets of E. granulosus (Figure 2).

editor_comments: Case distilled strictly to admission clinical presentation and initial cross-sectional imaging. Pathogen identification and surgical/microscopic findings quarantined to diagnostic reasoning.
